query: I work at a desk all day and have been having back pain. Would a standing desk actually help?
atoms: reduction of total daily sitting time
cost of desk vs cheaper alternatives
upper vs lower back pain distinction
standing fatigue and new pain risks
comparison to exercise and movement breaks
plausible_answers: Answer A (Movement Breaks Default): Skip the standing desk and focus on taking a 2–5 minute movement break every 30–45 minutes — evidence shows frequent movement reduces back pain more reliably than sit-stand desks, at zero cost.

Answer B (Standing Desk With Proper Setup): Get a sit-stand desk with anti-fatigue mat and proper ergonomic setup — used correctly with alternating postures every 30 minutes, it reduces upper back pain and prolonged sitting with meaningful evidence from long-term RCTs.

Answer C (Exercise Over Equipment): Invest time in a strength training program targeting core and hip stability rather than buying a standing desk — structural weakness is the primary driver of desk-related back pain and exercise addresses the root cause.
baseline_answer: Answer B (Standing Desk With Proper Setup): Get a sit-stand desk with anti-fatigue mat and proper ergonomic setup — used correctly with alternating postures every 30 minutes, it reduces upper back pain and prolonged sitting with meaningful evidence from long-term RCTs.
